text:
Aisha: Heads-up - Prospect Nimbus wants a Private/VPC POC next week. Requirements: SAML assertions must not traverse the public internet, prefer IPv6 for client traffic, and need a short non-tech justification PrivateLink vs Peering for their security reviewers. Can NetOps/Sec weigh in?

Tom: TL;DR: PrivateLink = endpoint isolation + narrower firewall rules. Peering = L3 reachability, cheaper, but broader exposure and more route mgmt. If SAML absolutely cannot leave their network, recommend either Private deployment or a tiny SAML proxy in their VPC that uses PrivateLink to our control plane.

Diego: IPv6 callout: our hosted PrivateLink connectors currently speak IPv4 only. We can support IPv6 for client-facing traffic via customer-side NAT64 or an IPv6-to-IPv4 gateway. Native IPv6-in-the-box is not GA yet; flag as potential blocker if they insist on native v6.

Aisha: They also want a minimal firewall allowlist and a note about TLS inspection.

Tom: Example firewall allowlist (placeholder CIDRs):
TCP 443 -> 35.180.200.0/22   # control-plane callbacks
TCP 443 -> 52.210.16.0/22   # model serving (hosted)
# If TLS inspection in place: allow SNI passthrough or install our cert on the inspection appliance

Diego: I'll gather exact CIDRs and static-egress EIP list for the call.

sec-bot: Prospect checked "no shared IPs". PrivateLink provides per-endpoint isolation but not guaranteed single-tenant hardware. If they require physical isolation, open a dedicated-hosting request.

Aisha: Thanks. Can we meet 2pm PT to finalize the checklist and send a one-page justification to their security reviewers?

Tom: 2pm works for me. Diego?

Diego: In. I'll bring CIDRs and a short NAT64 deployment note.

Aisha: Great, will schedule and send the draft checklist after the call. :thumbsup:
